name: International Typographic Style (Swiss Style)
visualIdentity: Supplemental design reference, not claimed as a directly named style in the source collection. Uses column and baseline grids, repeated spacing, asymmetric layouts, generous negative space, left-aligned sans-serif type, clear hierarchy, and grid-aligned photography.
suitableUses: Use alone for posters, identity, and typographic statements. It can also support UI and product storytelling, editorial layouts, motion posters, or staged geometry. Inference: it suits clear, concise communication where grid and type carry the message.
limitations: Adapt or omit a motion pattern if it obscures meaning, crops important details, forces text into unsafe areas, or disrupts page layout. Avoid carousel layouts when long-form reading or simultaneous comparison is needed. Supplemental provenance limits claims about canonical usage.
palette: Suggested new-artwork tokens only when task, brand, approved reference, and existing semantic colors are absent: white background #FFFFFF, black foreground #000000, restrained red accent #D32F2F. Keep discrete colors; gradients are disabled. Preserve supplied colors, roles, asset colors, and style color limits exactly; do not recolor or add hues. Check contrast in actual composited frames.
motionAndInteraction: Animate along horizontal or vertical layout axes and settle on shared alignment points without changing reading order. Preserve holds, deliberate cuts, and impacts. Interactive HTML may use finite scroll progress to recompose a pinned hero, scrub chapter handoffs, advance a narrative, or navigate a horizontal card track; provide keyboard/touch alternatives and reduced-motion states. Video must use authored seekable composition time, never live scroll or drag. Verify direct, backward, and sequential state evaluation.
audio: No fixed soundtrack or required audio layer. Choose music, voiceover, vocals, effects, ambience, or silence for the subject and audience; honor supplied assets and explicit requirements. Keep speech intelligible, avoid clipping or competing vocals, and synchronize picture and sound.
assetRequirements: Use loaded fonts, real text, and grid-aligned photographs. Build typography with CSS Grid; align SVG geometry to the baseline grid. Preload assets and fonts. For image lightboxes only, provide accurate dimensions, responsive sources, fallback links, and accessible navigation. State missing assets; do not imply simulated production is physical.
combinations: Swiss Style alone fits typographic statements. For verified data stories, a diagram/chart layer can share the grid, with only black, white, and red; use line weight or pattern for categories. For title sequences and manifestos, kinetic type can travel along column edges, using one sans-serif family and one red keyword per scene. These are optional combinations.
productionApproach: Choose visual and motion methods from the style and action first. HTML/CSS and SVG construct visuals; GSAP is the primary seekable motion engine, with Motion optional only when seeking is explicitly synchronized. HyperFrames handles composition, timing, media/audio sync, validation, and export; Remotion is allowed only if unavailable or a verified required capability is blocked, with reason recorded. Give each animated property one owner; use deterministic composition time. Inspect representative frames and decoded output.
